[June 2016]

After having a projected deorbit of 2013, but lasting three years longer, China's temporary space station, [Tiangong 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiangong-1), is finally set to deorbit. In its place, [Tiangong 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiangong-2) will be sent up, which will remain there for a couple of years, until the next stage of the mission is ready to launch.

[Tiangong 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiangong-1) spent its life as a space laboratory, used for gathering information for future projects, and for testing docking capabilities. The space station has had only two missions conducted to it, but each had provided priceless information. The missions, [Shenzhou 9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shenzhou_9) and [Shenzhou 10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shenzhou_10), while only lasting a few days, gave enough information for longer missions to happen with Tiangong 2.

[Tiangong 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiangong-2) plans to have more missions conducted on it, allowing the repository of knowledge China has in space to expand. With these missions, China will focus on the fine details of space life, for a future mission to the Red Planet.
